Verified_Outcome: Two subcutaneous xenograft models used athymic nude male mice, four treatment groups and n=6/group; fisetin 20 mg/kg i.p. three times/week, cabazitaxel 5 mg/kg i.p. once/week, combination, or vehicle. In the 22Rv1 model, the article reports tumor-growth inhibition of 14% with fisetin, 36% with cabazitaxel and 53% with the combination versus control. In the PC-3M-luc-6 model, after the reported 7-week treatment course, tumor volume increased 9-fold with the combination, 22-fold with fisetin, 20-fold with cabazitaxel and 32-fold with control; combination versus control and single agents p=0.0001 in Results. Body-weight monitoring showed no apparent combination toxicity, but the data were not shown. Methods state treatment began 2 weeks after implantation; Results state 3 days for the PC-3M model (V19-W11).
Remaining_Limitation: Animal xenograft results only; no clinical efficacy, human safety or dietary-exposure equivalence established. PC-3M treatment-start timing conflicts between Methods (2 weeks after implantation) and Results (3 days). Body-weight toxicity data are stated to be not shown; plotted tumor measurements were not digitized.

Verified_Outcome: Female nude mice (6–8 weeks) bearing subcutaneous SW620 tumors were randomized 5 days after inoculation to six groups (n=6/group). Ursolic acid 10 or 20 mg/kg i.p. was administered for five consecutive days; oxaliplatin was a single 10 mg/kg i.p. dose, alone or combined with ursolic acid. Tumor volume and body weight were monitored twice weekly; animals were sacrificed on day 50. Single agents reduced tumor weight versus vehicle (p<0.05); combination groups reduced it versus vehicle (p<0.01) and showed the strongest tumor inhibition. Oxaliplatin-associated serum ALT/AST elevations were reported as improved by ursolic acid; exact plotted values were not transcribed. Body weights were reported as maintained/improved, without exact figure values copied.
Remaining_Limitation: Animal model with one xenograft cell line and six mice per group; oxaliplatin was a single intraperitoneal dose. ALT/AST and tumor outcomes are figure based and were not digitized; no patient hepatoprotection, efficacy or dietary-exposure inference is supported. Source's claim of improved body weight is not quantified in text.
